## Effects of N-3 supplementation on indicies of metabolic syndrome 

Here we aim to model the sub-scores for the metabolic syndrome diagnostic criteria, along with related outcomes (@tbl-metsyn-scores). The goal is to build a model that imputes missing data to enable an intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis of all randomized participants. Imputation will allow for assessing the probability of meeting criteria thresholds for having at least 3 of 5 diagnostic criteria for metabolic syndrome in each treatment group while accounting for uncertainty associated with missing observations. @fig-descriptive-data shows distributions of the variables selected for joint modeling, including variables used to define metabolic syndrome. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-descriptive-data
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-cap: "Observed data distributions of main outcomes."



d_full <- criteria_dat |> 
  
  select(participant, time, treat, sex, age, analyte, value) |> 

  # Add missing values for all missing obs. 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = value) |> 

  pivot_longer(cols = c(T1, T2, T4), 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "time" ) |> 
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, 
              values_from = value) |> 

    pivot_longer(cols = HDL:Adiponectin, 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "analyte" ) |> 
  
  
  mutate(value_std = if_else(analyte == "TG", log(value), value)) |> 
  
  mutate(.by = analyte, 
         value_std = (value_std - mean(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 
  # To make all variables similarly signed HDL is reversed. 
  # Expected improvement in scores will be in the negative direction 
  # for all criteria markers
  mutate(participant = paste0("p", participant)) 

  


## Descriptive plots

d_full |> 
  mutate(
           analyte = case_when(
           analyte == "waist" ~ "Waist<br>circumference (cm)", 
           analyte == "glucose" ~ "Resting glucose<br>(mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)" ,
           analyte == "dias" ~ "Diastolic Blood pressure<br>(mmHg)", 
           analyte == "sys" ~ "Systolic Blood pressure<br>(mmHg)", 
           
           analyte == "TG" ~ "Triglycerides<br>(mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)", 
           analyte == "HDL" ~ "HDL Cholesterol<br>(mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)", 
           analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "Relative fat mass<br>(%)", 
           analyte == "bmi" ~ "Body mass index<br>(kg m<sup>-2</sup>)",
           analyte == "HOMA2IR" ~ "Insulin sensitivity<br>index", 
           analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "Adiponectin, &mu;g L<sup>-1</sup>"
           
         ), 
         sex = if_else(sex == "f", "Female", "Male")) |> 
  filter(!is.na(value)) |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(x = value, color = time)) + 
  geom_line(stat = "density") + 
  facet_wrap(~analyte + sex,  scales = "free")  + 
  alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) + 
  theme(strip.text = element_markdown(), 
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom") +
  labs(color = "Time") + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale)
```

Descriptive analysis of complete cases indicates variation in the proportion of participants meeting the criteria thresholds across treatment groups and post-intervention time points. @tbl-logregparticipants and  @fig-metsyndrome show the proportions of participants who have three or more diagnostic criteria for metabolic syndrome among complete cases. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-logregparticipants
#| tbl-cap: "Participants in the complete-case analysis of metabolic syndrome indications."


# Separate blood pressure critera
bp <- criteria_dat |> 
   filter((analyte %in% c("sys", "dias"))) |>   
  filter(participant %in% participant_complete_T4) |> 
 
  summarise(.by = c(participant, time, sex, treat, age), 
            crit = if_else(sum(crit) >= 1, 1, 0)) |> 
  mutate(analyte = "bp", 
         value = NA, 
         threshold = if_else(crit == 1, TRUE, FALSE)) |> 
  dplyr::select(participant, time, sex, analyte, value, 
                threshold, crit, treat, age) 


d <- criteria_dat |> 
  filter(!(analyte %in% c("sys", "dias"))) |> 
  filter(participant %in% participant_complete_T4) |> 
  bind_rows(bp) |> 
  
  
  
  summarise(.by = c(participant, time, treat, sex, age), 
            n = n(),
            n_threshold = sum(threshold, na.rm = TRUE) ) |> 
  
  mutate(met_syn = if_else(n_threshold >= 3, 1, 0), 
         age = (age - mean(age)) / sd(age)) 



# How many participants is in this analysis?
d |> 
  
  summarise(.by = c(time, treat, sex), 
            n = n(), 
            met_sym = sum(met_syn)) |> 
  arrange(time, treat) |> 
  
  
  mutate(n_prev = paste0(n, " (", round(100 * (met_sym/n), 0), "%)")) |> 
  select(-n, -met_sym) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = n_prev)  |> 
  
  mutate(sex = if_else(sex == "m", "Male", "Female"), 
         treat = if_else(treat == "ctrl", "Placebo", "N-3")) |> 
  
  bind_rows(
    d |> 
      
     summarise(.by = c(time, treat), 
            n = n(), 
            met_sym = sum(met_syn)) |> 
       arrange(time, treat) |> 
  
  
  mutate(n_prev = paste0(n, " (", round(100 * (met_sym/n), 0), "%)"))  |> 
  select(-n, -met_sym) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = n_prev)  |> 
  
  mutate(sex = "Total",
         treat = if_else(treat == "ctrl", "Placebo", "N-3")) |> 
  select(treat, sex, T1:T4) 
  ) |> 
  

  group_by(sex) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_markdown() |> 
  tab_spanner(label = "Time", 
              columns = 2:5) |> 
  
  cols_label(treat = "") |> 
  tab_footnote(footnote = "Data are presented as n (Metabolic syndrome proportion)")





```

Variables in the observed data are correlated within time points within variables and between variables across time points. To describe approximate variation and co-variation patterns, "naive" linear models were fitted with sex as a single predictor at time-point T1, sex, baseline values, and treatment as predictors for values at time-points T2 and T4. Residuals were extracted from the models, and estimates were plotted in @fig-var-cor. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-var-cor
#| fig-cap: "Residual variation and correlation pattern within and between variables in the observed data."
#| eval: true
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 12





d_full <- criteria_dat |> 
  select(participant, time, treat, sex, age, analyte, value) |>
  # Add missing values for all missing obs. 
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, 
              values_from = value) |> 

  pivot_longer(cols = c(T1, T2, T4), 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "time" ) |> 
  
  pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, 
              values_from = value) |> 

    pivot_longer(cols = HDL:Adiponectin, 
               values_to = "value",
               names_to = "analyte" ) |> 
  
  mutate(value_std = if_else(analyte %in% c("TG", "HOMA2IR"), log(value), value)) |> 
  

  
  mutate(.by = analyte, 
         value_std = (value_std - mean(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) |> 

  mutate(participant = paste0("p", participant)) 




# cor_plot is in helper.R
ps <- cor_plot(d_full)

(ps$p2 | ps$p1) / ps$p3



```

Correlation patterns among variables will be used to inform simulations (see @sec-synth-data). Correlations among variables also suggest that uncertainty associated with missing data can be reduced by exploiting the covariance among variables. The missing data patterns of the observed data indicate that some missing data occurs in a single variable at a single time point whilst some participants have missing data in all variables at specific time points (@fig-missing-data).

To assess if the outcome variables predict drop-out we fit a logistic regression model with drop-out ($D_i$) at time $\text{Time}$ T2 or T4, coded as 0/1 as the outcome variable. The association between the standardized measurement type value ($X_{i[A]}$) and drop-out was determined while controlling for sex ($S$) within each treatment group ($T$).

$$
\begin{align}
D_{i[\text{Time}]} &\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_i) \\
\operatorname{Logit}(p_i) &= \alpha_{[A]} + \beta_{X[A]} X_{i[A]} + \beta_{S[A]} S_i + \beta_{T[A]} T_i + \beta_{TX[A]} T_i X_i \\
\alpha_{[A]} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 0.5) \\
\beta_{X[A]} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 0.5) \\
\beta_{S[A]} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 0.5) \\
\beta_{T[A]} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 0.5) \\
\beta_{TX[A]} &\sim \operatorname{Normal}(0, 0.5) 
\end{align}
$$



```{r}
#| label: missing-data-prep


miss_dat <- criteria_dat |> 
  select(- threshold, -crit) |> 
  # Filter for time-point 1
  filter(time == "T1") |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = analyte, 
              values_from = value) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = age:Adiponectin, 
               values_to = "value", 
               names_to = "analyte")  |> 
    mutate(.by = analyte, 
         value_std = if_else(analyte %in% c("TG", "HOMA2IR"), log(value), value), 
         value_std = (value_std - mean(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(value_std, na.rm = TRUE)) 

## For mean-centering 
baseline_cent <- miss_dat |> 
  summarise(.by = analyte, 
            m = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), 
            s = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), 
            nas = sum(is.na(value_std)), 
            n = n()) |> 
  mutate(nas = nas / n) 


miss_dat2 <- miss_dat |> 
  filter(!is.na(value_std)) |> 
  # Missing at follow-up
  mutate(
    miss_t4 = if_else(participant %in% participant_complete_T4, 0, 1), 
    miss_t2 = if_else(participant %in% participant_complete_T2, 0, 1), 
    P = dense_rank(participant), 
    A = dense_rank(analyte), 
    TX= if_else(treat == "ctrl", -0.5, 0.5), 
    S = if_else(sex == "m", -0.5, 0.5),
  ) 
  
  
# Prepare list for model 
d <- list(
  N = nrow(miss_dat2), 
  N_A = length(unique(miss_dat2$A)), 
  N_P = length(unique(miss_dat2$P)), 
  N_TX =length(unique(miss_dat2$TX)), 
  N_S = length(unique(miss_dat2$S)), 
  # Indicators
  P = miss_dat2$P,           # Participant
  A = miss_dat2$A,           # Outcome/Analyte
  TX= miss_dat2$TX,          # Treatment
  
  # Predictors
  S = miss_dat2$S,           # sex
  x = miss_dat2$value_std,   # outcome std value
  do4 = miss_dat2$miss_t4,   # Drop-out to T4 
  do2 = miss_dat2$miss_t2,    # Drop-out to T2
  
  prior_only = 1
  
)
```


```{r}
#| label: model1-fit
#| output: false

# Compiling the model
m1 <- cmdstan_model(stan_file = "models/m1.stan", 
                      exe_file = "models/m1.exe")



fit_wrap(m1,fit = "fit.m1", DATA = d)

```

In addition to measurements included in the metabolic syndrome diagnostic criteria (Fasting glucose, waist circumference, HDL, triglycerides, blood pressure), we also included relative fat mass, body mass index, age and insulin resistance index (HOMA2IR) and adiponectin. Prior predictive checks (@fig-dropout-priorpredictive) confirmed that the model expects eleven measurement types in two treatment groups and that the combined priors weakly regularize away from all/non drop-out.


```{r}
#| label: fig-dropout-priorpredictive
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-cap: "Prior predictive simulation for model 1. Columns are values of the predictor (SD-units) rows represents each predictor."


draws.m1 <- fit.m1$draws(format = "df")


draws.m1 |> 
  filter(.chain == 1) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with(c("alpha2", "beta2"))) |> 
  separate(name, into = c("param", "A"), sep = "\\[") |> 
  mutate(A = gsub("\\]", "", A)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, 
              values_from = value) |> 
  # Adding predictor variables
  expand_grid(x = seq(from = -3, to = 3, by = 3), 
                TX = c(-0.5, 0.5)) |>
  
  mutate(log_odds = alpha2 + beta2_x * x + beta2_tx * TX + beta2_xtx * TX * x, 
         prob = plogis(log_odds)) |> 
  mutate(Treatment = if_else(TX == -0.5, "Placebo", "N-3")) |> 
  ggplot(aes(prob, color = Treatment)) + 
  geom_line(stat = "density") +
  facet_grid( A ~ x ) +
  labs(x = "Drop-out probability", 
       y = "Prior density") +
  theme_classic() + 
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), 
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0)) + 
  scale_color_manual(values = colscale)

  
```



```{r}
#| output: false
#| label: m1-posterior-fit

d$prior_only <- 0
fit_wrap(m1, fit = "fit.m1p", DATA = d)
draws.m1 <- fit.m1p$draws(format = "df")

```


```{r}
#| label: fig-dropout-across
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-cap: "Probability of drop-out across values of baseline co-variates on per treatment group to time-point 2 (A) and 4 (B). Estimates are adjusted for sex, intervals are 90% percentile interval."

a <- draws.m1 |> 
  filter(.chain == 1) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with(c("alpha2", "beta2"))) |> 
  separate(name, into = c("param", "A"), sep = "\\[") |> 
  mutate(A = gsub("\\]", "", A)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, 
              values_from = value) |> 
  # Adding predictor variables
  expand_grid(x = seq(from = -3, to = 3, by = 0.1), 
                TX = c(-0.5, 0.5)) |>
  
  mutate(log_odds = alpha2 + beta2_x * x + beta2_tx * TX + beta2_xtx * TX * x, 
         prob = plogis(log_odds), 
         Treatment = if_else(TX == -0.5, "Placebo", "N-3")) |> 
  

  summarise(.by = c(A, Treatment, x), 
            mprob = mean(prob), 
            lwr = quantile(prob, 0.05), 
            upr = quantile(prob, 0.95)) |> 
  
  # Inner join transforming to centering
  inner_join(
    miss_dat2 |> 
  distinct(A, analyte) |> 
  mutate(
    
    A = as.character(A),
    
    Outcome = case_when(
    analyte == "age" ~ "Age (years)", 
    analyte == "waist" ~ "Waist circumference (cm)", 
    analyte == "glucose" ~ "Resting glucose (mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)" ,
    analyte == "dias" ~ "Diastolic blood pressure (mmHg)", 
    analyte == "sys" ~ "Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)", 
    analyte == "TG" ~ "Triglycerides (log mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)", 
    analyte == "HDL" ~ "HDL Cholesterol (mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)", 
    analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "Relative fat mass (%)", 
    analyte == "bmi" ~ "Body mass index (kg m<sup>-2</sup>)",
    analyte == "HOMA2IR" ~ "Insulin resistance index (log)", 
    analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "Adiponectin (mg L<sup>-1</sup>)")) |> 
  inner_join(
    baseline_cent
   )
  ) |> 
  
  mutate(outcome_scale = m + x * s) |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(outcome_scale, mprob, 
             fill = Treatment,
             ymin = lwr, ymax = upr)) +
  geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.2) + 
  facet_wrap(~ Outcome, scales = "free_x") + 
  
  theme(strip.text = element_markdown(), 
        legend.position = c(0.9, 0.96), 
        legend.title = element_blank()) + 
  labs(x = "", 
       y = "Probability of drop-out", 
       title = "A") 
  


b <- draws.m1 |>

  mutate(A = gsub("\\]", "", A)) |>
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dropout
#| tbl-cap: "Change in log-odds (Slope) for drop-out for 1 SD-unit change in baseline characteristic (Outcome) and differences in slope between treatment groups (&Delta Treatment) at time T2 and time T4. Values are posterior means with 95% percentile intervals."


draws.m1 |> 
  filter(.chain == 1) |> 
  select(.iteration, starts_with("beta")) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with(c("beta"))) |> 
  separate(name, into = c("param", "A"), sep = "\\[") |> 
  mutate(A = gsub("\\]", "", A)) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, 
              values_from = value) |> 

  mutate(
    avg_t2 = beta2_x,   # avg log odds effect of baseline t2
    avg_t4 = beta4_x,   # avg log odds ... t4
    txd_t2 = beta2_xtx, # diff in slope between tx groups t2
    txd_t4 = beta4_xtx, # diff in slope between tx groups t2
      ) |> 
  
    select(A, avg_t2:txd_t4) |> 
    pivot_longer(cols = avg_t2:txd_t4) |> 
  
  
  summarise(.by = c(A, name), 
            mlo = mean(value), 
            lwr = quantile(value, 0.025), 
            upr = quantile(value, 0.975)) |> 
  
  mutate(stat = paste0(sprintf("%.2f", round(mlo, 2)), 
                       " [", 
                       sprintf("%.2f", round(lwr, 2)), 
                       ", ", 
                       sprintf("%.2f", round(upr, 2)), 
                       "]"), 
         A = as.integer(A)) |> 
  dplyr::select(A, name, stat) |> 
  inner_join(
    miss_dat2 |> 
      distinct(A, analyte) |> 
      mutate(
    Outcome = case_when(
    analyte == "age" ~ "Age (years)", 
    analyte == "waist" ~ "Waist circumference (cm)", 
    analyte == "glucose" ~ "Resting glucose (mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)" ,
    analyte == "dias" ~ "Diastolic blood pressure (mmHg)", 
    analyte == "sys" ~ "Systolic blood pressure (mmHg)", 
    analyte == "TG" ~ "Triglycerides (log mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)", 
    analyte == "HDL" ~ "HDL Cholesterol (mmol L<sup>-1</sup>)", 
    analyte == "fat.rel" ~ "Relative fat mass (%)", 
    analyte == "bmi" ~ "Body mass index (kg m<sup>-2</sup>)",
    analyte == "HOMA2IR" ~ "Insulin resistance index (log)", 
    analyte == "Adiponectin" ~ "Adiponectin (mg L<sup>-1</sup>)"))) |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, 
              values_from = stat) |> 
  dplyr::select(Outcome, avg_t2, txd_t2, avg_t4, txd_t4) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_markdown(columns = Outcome) |> 
  tab_spanner(label = "T2", 
              columns = c(avg_t2, txd_t2)) |> 
  tab_spanner(label = "T4", 
              columns = c(avg_t4, txd_t4)) |> 
  cols_label(
    avg_t2 = "Slope",
    txd_t2 = md("&Delta; Treatment"), 
    avg_t4 = "Slope",
    txd_t4 = md("&Delta; Treatment")
    ) |> 
  opt_table_font( font = list(
      google_font(name = "Merriweather"),
      "Cochin", "serif"
    ), 
    size = 10)
  
```

In conclusion, age was negatively associated with probability of drop-out at T2 without robust difference between treatment groups (@fig-dropout-across A; @tbl-dropout). Resting glucose at baseline tended to predict drop-out to T4 with no strong difference between treatment groups (@fig-dropout-across B; @tbl-dropout). Together this suggest that baseline covariates did not robustly interact with treatment in predicting drop-out. However, baseline covariates (age and fasting glucose) were associated with higher drop-out rates.

### Synthetic data {#sec-synth-data}

Synthetic data is generated with known parameter values to validate models and to explore the effects of model misspecification and missing data. The first data simulation function uses a multivariate normal distribution to simulate conditional means for *K* measurement types and *N* participants.

$$
\begin{align}
y_{i,j} &\sim \operatorname{MVNormal}(\mu_{k[i,j]}, \Sigma) \\
\mu_{k[i,j]} &= \alpha + \beta_k X
\end{align}
$$

Where $y_{i,j}$ is a vector of outcome values for participant *i* in time-point *j*, drawn from a multivariate normal distribution with conditional means ($\mu_{k[i,j]}$ and a variance-covariance matrix ($\Sigma$). The conditional means are simulated using a linear predictor with parameter vector $\beta$ and design matrix $X$.

The covariance matrix is constructed from two separate correlation matrices and a cross-time-point vector of correlations within each measurement type. Residual standard deviations for each type (and time) are used to combine standard deviations and correlations into the variance-covariance matrix[^note-on-code].   

$$
\begin{align}
\rho_{t2} &=  \begin{bmatrix}
  1 & \rho_{12} & \cdots \\
  \rho_{21} & 1 & \cdots \\
  \vdots & \vdots & \ddots
\end{bmatrix} \\
\rho_{t4} &=  \begin{bmatrix}
  1 & \rho_{12} & \cdots \\
  \rho_{21} & 1 & \cdots \\
  \vdots & \vdots & \ddots
\end{bmatrix} \\
\rho_{\text{cross}} &= \operatorname{diag}(p_{k,\text{time}}) \\
R &=  \begin{bmatrix}
  \rho_{t2} & \rho_{\text{cross}} \\
  \rho_{\text{cross}}^T & \rho_{t4} \\
  \end{bmatrix} \\
S &= \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_{k,\text{time}}) \\
\Sigma &= S \times R \times S
\end{align}
$$

We will be able to control the within-time *residual* correlations between measurement types and between-time *residual* correlations within measurement types. The full correlation matrix ($R$) will set the residual correlation between measurement types at different time points to 0. These will, however, be correlated through within-time-point and pre-intervention correlations.

The pre-intervention values are also conditionally constructed using a separate multivariate normal distribution. 

$$
\begin{align}
y_{\text{pre}[i]} &\sim \operatorname{MVNormal}(\mu_{k[i]}, \Sigma) \\
\mu_{k[i]} &= \alpha + \beta_k X \\
R &=  \begin{bmatrix}
  1 & \rho_{12} & \cdots \\
  \rho_{21} & 1 & \cdots \\
  \vdots & \vdots & \ddots
\end{bmatrix} \\
S &= \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_{k}) \\
\Sigma &= S \times R \times S \\
\end{align}
$$
Using this definition, we can control the correlations among measurement types (at baseline) and their variation. We can also make the means conditional on a set of predictors (design matrix $X$) with corresponding parameter values ($\beta_k$).

[^note-on-code]: In the simulation function (`./R/sim-fun/sim-type.R`) separate variance-covariance matrices are constructed and then combined. But separate correlation matrices are the function's input. 

The approach detailed above is convenient as we are able to define each pairwise correlation. However, this comes with two caveats. First, for 8 variables we need to set $((8 \times 8 - 8) / 2) \times 3 = 84$ correlation coefficients to capture between variable correlations at each time-point. Second, this approach does not guarantee a positive definite covariance matrix. An alternative is to use a factor loading approach[^note-on-factor]. For each variable we can specify a loading onto a factor and a residual variance for each variable (type). This approach is determined by $\lambda$, a $K \times F$ matrix where $k_i$ are variables and $f_j$ are latent factors, and $\psi$, a vector of length $K$ defining residual variation.

[^note-on-factor]: See [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factor_analysis) for an introduction on the maths. 

$$
\begin{align}
\Sigma_\text{raw} &= \lambda \times \lambda^T + \text{diag}(\psi) \\
D &= \sqrt{\text{diag}(\Sigma_\text{raw})} \\
R &= D^{-1} \times \Sigma_\text{raw} \times D^{-1} \\ 
S &= \operatorname{diag}(\sigma_{k}) \\
\Sigma &= S \times R \times  S
\end{align}
$$

This approach is used in `sim_type2` where $\Sigma$ is built from the factor approach. Lambda is a matrix with K rows, representing variable types and F columns representing factors.

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

build_sigma_factor <- function(Lambda, psi, S) {
  K <- nrow(Lambda)
  R_raw <- Lambda %*% t(Lambda) + diag(psi)
  d <- sqrt(diag(R_raw))
  R <- R_raw / outer(d, d)
  diag(S) %*% R %*% diag(S)
}

```

As an example, $K=5$ variable types are defined using $F=3$ factors below. Approximate "variance explained" can be used to define the relationship between variables and factors where for $k_1$ we aim for 50%, 20% and 10% explained by $f_1$ to $f_3$ and the remaining 20% is error. The squared loadings plus error sum to 1: $0.5 + 0.2 + 0.1 + 0.2 = 1$. In code: 

```{r}
#| echo: true

# Loadings as proportions
l1 <- c(0.5,  0.2,  0.1)
# Transforms to loadings
l1 <- sqrt(l1)
error <- 0.2

sum(l1^2) + error

```

The above example first defines loadings as proportions (summing to 1 with errors) and then adds a step to transform the proportions to loadings. For a full $K \times F$ &lambda; matrix we populate the matrix and use &psi; for errors.

```{r}
#| echo: true


# Defining a matrix of proportions explained by factors
Lambda <- matrix(
  c(0.5, 0.2, 0.1,
    0.8, 0.1, 0.05,  
    0.1, 0.15, 0.1,
    0.05, 0.05, 0.2,
    0.05, 0.1, 0.01
    ), 
                 ncol = 3,
                 byrow = TRUE)
# Defining remaining error
psi <- c(0.2, 0.05, 0.65, 0.7, 0.84)

# Transform from proportions to loadings
Lambda <- sqrt(Lambda)

# Check total proportions
rowSums(Lambda^2) + psi

```

Each row of the &lambda; matrix plus errors now sum to 1. Next, we can use the &lambda; matrix to construct $\Sigma$ with unit standard deviations. The full covariance matrix ($\Sigma$) is used in calling `MASS::mvnorm` to produce the multivariate normal variable. As we are using standard deviations equal to 1, the covariance matrix equals the correlation matrix.

```{r}
#| echo: true

S <- rep(1, 5)
Sigma <- build_sigma_factor(Lambda, psi, S)

out <- MASS::mvrnorm(1000, rep(0, 5), Sigma = Sigma)

colnames(out) <- paste0("k", 1:5)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sigma-out
#| tbl-cap: "Correlations used to simulate data built using a factor approach."
colnames(Sigma) <-  paste0("k", 1:5)
rownames(Sigma) <-  paste0("k", 1:5)

data.frame(Sigma) |> 
  gt(rownames_to_stub = TRUE) |> 
  fmt_number(decimals = 3)

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-corr-out
#| tbl-cap: "Correlations from simulated data (n=1000) built using a factor approach."

data.frame(out) |> 
  correlate(quiet = TRUE) |> 
  gt() |> 
  fmt_number(decimals = 3)

```

In the loadings we defined $k_1$ and $k_2$ to be highly correlated through being influenced to a large degree by factors $f_1$ and $f_2$. In contrast, $k_5$ was given a lot of variation not explained by the factors which resulted in lower correlations with the other variables.


#### Heteroscedasticity and non-normal noise

The synthetic data-generating models described above produces homoscedastic data, i.e., equal residual variation between treatment groups. To create synthetic data under heteroscedastic conditions (unequal variance between treatment groups) an additional data generating model is created to enable setting treatment-specific variation (`sim_type3` function in `R/sim-fun.R`). The `sim_type3` function also includes two arguments to set additional noise in post-treatment measurements `prop_noise` controls the fraction of measurements that gets extra noise added and `sd_noise` controls the zero-centered normal distribution from which additional noise is drawn.  

#### Missing data

Two mechanisms for including missing values are used in the simulation functions. First, a proportion of pre- and post-intervention values are set to missing, affecting single observations (e.g., a single measurement within a single participant). Second, the probability of missing observations from a whole participant is simulated using a Bernoulli model. This mechanism can connect baseline predictors to missing values. A Bernoulli simulation is performed, with $p_i$ modeled linearly by $\alpha$, which controls the average probability of complete missing observations, and the additional parameters $\beta$ linked to predictors in a predictor data frame.

$$
\begin{align}
y_{\text{miss}[i]} &\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_i) \\
\operatorname{logit}(p_i) &= \alpha + \beta X
\end{align}
$$

Simulating a full (K = 8) data set of synthetic data, with missing values, results in observed patterns similar to the observed data (@fig-missing-data, @fig-synth-data-example and @fig-synth-data-missing).


```{r}
#| label: synthetic-data-example
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

  N <- 148 # Number of participants
  K <- 8 # number of measurement types

  # The formula for the pre-intervention variables
  form_pre <- ~ 1 +  age + sex

  # beta_pre is a p * K matrix of parameter (p in 1 to P)
  # values for each type (k in 1:K).
  # fmt: skip
  betas_pre <- matrix(
  c(rep(0, K), # intercepts
    0.2, -0.2, 0.1, -0.1, 0.1, -0.1, 0, 0,  # age
    0.2, -0.2, 0, 0, -0.2, 0.2, 0, 0  # sex
  ),
  nrow = 3,
  ncol = K,
  byrow = TRUE
)

  # The same formula for both time-points
  form_main <- ~  pre + group + sex

  # betas matrix are p * K
  # fmt: skip
  betas_t1 <- matrix(
  c(rep(0, K), # intercepts
    0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.86, 0.85, 0.86, 0.85,  # pre_k effect 
    0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, # group
    0.1, 0.2, -0.1, -0.2, 0.1, 0.2, 0.1, 0.1  # sex
  ),
  nrow = 4,
  ncol = K,
  byrow = TRUE
)

  # fmt: skip
  betas_t2 <- matrix(
  c(rep(0, K), # intercepts
   0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.95, 0.86, 0.85, 0.86, 0.85,  # pre_k effect 
    0, 0.4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, # group
    0.1, 0.2, -0.1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0  # sex
  ),
  nrow = 4,
  ncol = K,
  byrow = TRUE
)

  
  
  # Predictor variables, used in *all* sims
  preds_all <- data.frame(
    group = rep(c(0, 1), each = N / 2),
    sex = rep(c(0, 1),  N/2 ),
    age = c(runif(N/2, -1.5, 1.5), rnorm(N/2))
  )

  # Vector of correlations (upper triangle, fill by column) for the pre int
  # values. For a K = 8 matrix, this should be (K * K - K) / 2 = 
  # (8 * 8 - 8) / 2
  c1 <- c(
    # E.g., type 1 correlation with type 2 = r12
    0.2,     # r12
    0.2,     # r13
    0.6,     # r23
    0,     # r14
    0,     # r24
    0,     # r34
    0,     # r15
    0,     # r25
    0,     # r35
    0,     # r45
    0,     # r16
    0,     # r26
    0,     # r36
    0,     # r46
    0,     # r56
    0,     # r17
    0,     # r27
    0.2,     # r37
    0.2,     # r47
    0.3,     # r57
    0.5,     # r67
    0.4,     # r18
    0,     # r28
    0,     # r38
    0,     # r48
    0,     # r58
    0,     # r68
    0      # r78
  )

  # A list of two (per time-point) residual correlations
  # (upper triangle, fill by row)
  c2 <- list(
    c(
    # E.g., type 1 correlation with type 2 = r12
    0,     # r12
    0,     # r13
    0,     # r23
    0,     # r14
    0,     # r24
    0,     # r34
    0,     # r15
    0,     # r25
    0,     # r35
    0,     # r45
    0,     # r16
    0,     # r26
    0,     # r36
    0,     # r46
    0,     # r56
    0,     # r17
    0,     # r27
    0,     # r37
    0,     # r47
    0,     # r57
    0,     # r67
    0,     # r18
    0,     # r28
    0,     # r38
    0,     # r48
    0,     # r58
    0,     # r68
    0      # r78
  ),
    c(
    # E.g., type 1 correlation with type 2 = r12
    0,     # r12
    0,     # r13
    0,     # r23
    0,     # r14
    0,     # r24
    0,     # r34
    0,     # r15
    0,     # r25
    0,     # r35
    0,     # r45
    0,     # r16
    0,     # r26
    0,     # r36
    0,     # r46
    0,     # r56
    0,     # r17
    0,     # r27
    0,     # r37
    0,     # r47
    0,     # r57
    0,     # r67
    0,     # r18
    0,     # r28
    0,     # r38
    0,     # r48
    0,     # r58
    0,     # r68
    0      # r78
  )
  )

  # Pre intervention SD's per type (length K)
  s1 <- rep(1, K)
  # Residual SD per type in each time point
  s2 <- list(
    c(0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1),
     c(0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 0.8, 0.9, 1, 1.1)
  )
  # Between time-point (residual) correlations within each type (length K)
  c_cross <- c(rep(0.5, K))

  # missing_form_t2,  formula specifying the predictor for missing values at t2
  miss_t2 <- ~ 1 + age
  miss_t4 <- ~ 1 + age

  # Parameter values for the form complete missingness
  miss_beta_t2 <- c(-2.5, -0.5)
  miss_beta_t4 <- c(-2, -0.5)

  # Random missing proportion
  miss_prop_pre <- 0.02 # e.g., 2% missing of all rows
  miss_prop_y <- 0.05 # e.g., 5% miss of all rows post-int

  
  # The simulation function
  simout <- sim_type(
    
    n = N,
    K = K,

    form_pre = form_pre,
    betas_pre = betas_pre,

    form = form_main,
    preds = preds_all,
    betas = list(betas_t1, betas_t2),
    C1 = c1,
    S1 = s1,
    C2 = c2,
    S2 = s2,
    C_cross = c_cross,
    missing_form_t2 = miss_t2,
    missing_form_t4 = miss_t4,
    missing_beta_t2 = miss_beta_t2,
    missing_beta_t4 = miss_beta_t4,
    missing_pre_prop = miss_prop_pre,
    missing_y_prop = miss_prop_y,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
```

```{r}
 # Sum up n missing values
  mutate(.by = participant, 
         n_miss =  sum(is.na(y))) |> 
  # Sort participants per missingness
 mutate(participant = fct_reorder(as.factor(participant), -n_miss)) |>
  
 mutate(miss = if_else(is.na(y), "miss", "data"),
        miss = factor(miss, levels = c("data", "miss"), 
                       labels = c("Observed data", 
                                  "Missing data"))) |> 
  # dense rank within group
  mutate(.by = group, 
         participant = dense_rank(participant)) |> 

  # Per group
  ggplot(aes(type, participant, 
             color = miss, 
             fill = as.factor(type), 
             alpha = miss)) + 
  

  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 2) + 

  scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "gray")) + 
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(1, 0.6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = colscale) + 
  facet_nested( ~ group + time , scales = "free_y") +

  alpha_theme(yaxis = FALSE) +
  
  
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
        axis.ticks.y  = element_blank(), 
        axis.text.x = element_blank(), 
        axis.ticks.x  = element_blank(), 
        axis.line.x = element_blank(), 
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = c("gray90"))
        ) + 
  labs(x = "",
       y = "", 
       fill = "Measurement", 
       color = "", 
       alpha = "")



```
